questions.stem: What moisture content is required for honey to prevent fermentation?

options.B: Not greater than 17%

questions.explanation: To prevent fermentation, the moisture content of the honey must not be greater than 17%.

questions.stem: How does the provided manual define modern bee keeping (apiculture)?

options.A: The traditional hunting of honey in natural forests
options.B: The art and practice of rearing bees in man-made containers called hives
options.C: The process of extracting honey from wild hollow logs using fire
options.D: The study of wild bee flight patterns in the tropics

questions.explanation: According to the text, modern bee keeping or apiculture is specifically defined as the practice of rearing bees in artificial or man-made containers/boxes known as hives.

questions.stem: What is a primary advantage of modern beekeeping over traditional honey hunting mentioned in the text?

options.B: It allows for the destruction of bees by fire
options.C: It does not involve the destruction of honey bees by fire
options.D: It can only be practiced by professional scientists

questions.explanation: The main advantage cited for modern methods is that it avoids the destruction of honey bees by fire, which is a common characteristic of traditional honey hunting.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a benefit of bee keeping in the manual?

options.A: Crop pollination resulting in increased seed yields
options.B: Income generation from the sale of venom and propolis
options.C: Requirement of high capital and intensive daily labor
options.D: Apitherapeutic uses for treating ailments like arthritis

questions.explanation: The manual explicitly states that beekeeping is NOT capital-intensive (low capital requirement) and does NOT require much time or daily attention.

questions.stem: Why is beekeeping considered suitable for 'marginal lands'?

options.A: Bees prefer land that is heavily chemically treated
options.B: Such lands may be otherwise un-useful for standard agricultural purposes
options.C: Bees require land that is frequently flooded
options.D: Beekeeping requires extensive land clearing and preparation

questions.explanation: The text notes that beekeeping can be established on small or marginal lands that are typically not useful for other agricultural purposes.

questions.stem: According to the biology of honey bees, how many wings and legs do they possess?

options.B: Two wings and six legs

questions.explanation: The manual describes the honey bee body as having six legs and four wings.

questions.stem: What are the four stages of the honey bee life cycle in order?

options.B: Egg, larva, pupa, adult

questions.explanation: Honey bees undergo complete metamorphosis, which follows the sequence: egg-larva-pupa-adult.

questions.stem: Which caste of the honey bee colony is responsible for producing Pheromones (queen substance)?

options.B: Workers

questions.explanation: The queen is a fully developed and fertilized female that produces eggs and queen substance (pheromones) to maintain the colony.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of Drones within the honey bee colony?

options.A: Cleaning the hive and foraging for nectar
options.B: Defending the hive against invaders
options.D: Tending to the brood and feeding the queen

questions.explanation: The text states that drones are males whose main purpose is to mate with a virgin queen.

questions.stem: Which type of hive is specifically recommended for commercial honey production?

options.B: Hollow log hives
options.C: Removable comb hives with top bars
options.D: Removable comb hives with frames (e.g., Langstroth hive)

questions.explanation: The manual explicitly recommends removable comb hives with frames, such as the Langstroth hive, for commercial honey production.

questions.stem: Which of the following is considered a 'baiting material' used to attract a natural swarm?

options.B: Palm wine juice

questions.explanation: Palm wine juice is listed among the materials (like honey, jam, and bee wax) used as baiting materials to attract honeybees to a hive.

questions.stem: When should supplementary feeding (sugar syrup or fruit juice) be provided to bees?

options.A: Only during the peak honey flow season
options.B: During the 'dearth period' when nectar and pollen are scarce
options.C: Every day regardless of the season
options.D: Only when the queen is laying eggs

questions.explanation: Supplementary feeding is provided during the dearth period (scarcity of nectar/pollen) to prevent swarming or absconding and ensure future yields.

questions.stem: In the tropical seasonal management calendar, which months correspond to the 'Honey flow/harvesting season'?

options.B: June - August

questions.explanation: The manual identifies December to March as the honey flow/harvesting season in the tropical region.

questions.stem: Why is a smoker considered the 'beekeeper's companion'?

options.A: It helps the beekeeper see in the dark
options.B: It reduces bee stings and keeps them calm during inspection
options.C: It is used to kill the bees before harvesting
options.D: It provides warmth to the bee brood

questions.explanation: Smoking bees reduces stings and keeps them calm, allowing the beekeeper to remain in control while working.

questions.stem: What is the difference between 'Swarming' and 'Absconding'?

options.A: Swarming is due to pests; absconding is due to a new queen
options.B: Swarming is a reproductive process where part of the colony leaves; absconding is when the entire colony abandons the hive
options.C: Swarming involves the death of the queen; absconding involve the death of drones
options.D: There is no difference; they are synonymous terms

questions.explanation: The text defines swarming as a reproductive process where a queen and some workers leave, while absconding is when the queen and all other bees leave the hive completely.

questions.stem: Which of these factors is most likely to anger bees during a routine inspection?

options.A: Wearing a smooth white protective suit
options.B: Presence of an active laying queen
options.C: Standing or working in front of the path of the hive

questions.explanation: Standing in the flight path of the bees is listed as an activity that can anger them during inspection.

questions.stem: Why are metals avoided for packaging honey?

options.A: Metals make the honey too heavy to transport
options.B: Mineral reactions occur that destroy the texture, color, and quality
options.C: Metals are more expensive than glass or plastic
options.D: Metals make the honey ferment faster than plastic

questions.explanation: Metals are not used because mineral reactions occur that cause the destruction of the honey's texture, color, and quality.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a physical test for identifying pure/unadulterated honey?

options.A: It dissolves instantly when dropped in water
options.B: It spreads like water when dropped on sand
options.C: It remains intact and has a slow solution when mixed with water (until stirred)
options.D: It turns blue when exposed to the sun

questions.explanation: Pure honey does not mix with water immediately; it remains intact until stirred.

questions.stem: Which of the following are mentioned as bee 'pests' in the manual?

options.B: Varroa mite, wax moth, and ants

questions.explanation: Varroa mite, wax moth, ants, termites, cattle, and game are listed as pests.

questions.stem: A beekeeper notices several queen cells in a hive and wants to prevent the colony from splitting. What action is recommended?

options.A: Increase the temperature of the hive
options.B: Destruction of extra queen cells

questions.explanation: To prevent swarming (the reproductive splitting of the colony), one of the recommended methods is the destruction of extra queen cells.

questions.stem: Which body part of the honey bee contains the wings and legs?

options.B: Thorax

questions.explanation: The thorax of insects bears the legs and wings.

questions.stem: Approximately how many worker bees are typically present in a colony according to the manual?

options.B: About 2,000

questions.explanation: The manual states that about 20,000 worker bees are present in a colony.

questions.stem: Which caste performs foraging, cleaning, defense, and tending of the queen?

options.B: Workers

questions.explanation: Workers carry out all activities inside and outside the hive.

questions.stem: Why are removable comb hives with top bars considered suitable for beginners?

options.A: They are cheaper than traditional hives
options.B: They are easier to handle and manage
options.C: They produce more honey than frame hives

questions.explanation: The manual states they are readily handled by beginners.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a factor to consider when locating an apiary?

options.B: Proximity to chemical pollution

questions.explanation: Areas should be free from agro and industrial chemical poisoning.

questions.stem: A beekeeper sets up hives in a flood-prone area. What is the most likely consequence?

options.B: Improved ventilation

questions.explanation: Apiaries should be located away from flood-prone or waterlogged areas.

questions.stem: Which method of acquiring bees involves attracting a natural swarm using sweet substances?

options.B: Purchase of nucleus colony

questions.explanation: Baiting involves using sweet materials to attract bees into a hive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is classified as a DISEASE rather than a pest?

options.B: Nosema

questions.explanation: Nosema is listed under diseases of honey bees.

questions.stem: Which season in the tropical calendar corresponds to nectar flow?

options.B: June - August

questions.explanation: Nectar flow season occurs between September and November.

questions.stem: Why should only capped honey combs be harvested?

options.A: Uncapped combs contain immature honey with high moisture
options.B: Capped combs are easier to cut

questions.explanation: Mature honey is sealed with wax and has safe moisture levels.

questions.stem: Which equipment is specifically used to prevent the queen from entering certain hive sections?

options.B: Queen excluder

questions.explanation: A queen excluder prevents the queen from accessing certain areas of the hive.

questions.stem: Why is strict cleanliness important during honey processing?

options.B: To avoid contamination and poisoning

questions.explanation: The manual emphasizes strict cleanliness during handling.

questions.stem: Which of the following activities can reduce the risk of swarming?

options.B: Destroying extra queen cells

questions.explanation: Destruction of extra queen cells helps prevent swarming.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an entrepreneurial opportunity in beekeeping?

options.B: Pollination service for fees

questions.explanation: Pollination service is listed as an income opportunity.

questions.stem: A beekeeper notices persistent disturbance and overheating in the hive. What is the likely outcome?

options.B: Swarming or absconding

questions.explanation: Environmental stressors such as high temperature and disturbance can cause swarming or absconding.

questions.stem: A farmer wants to start beekeeping on a small budget. Which characteristic of beekeeping, as listed in the manual, directly supports this goal?

options.A: It requires daily attention to be profitable
options.B: It is capital-intensive with high startup costs
options.C: It involves low capital requirement and equipment can be improvised
options.D: It requires large tracts of land for the apiary

questions.explanation: The manual states beekeeping is NOT capital-intensive and that equipment/tools can be improvised from locally available and cheap materials.

questions.stem: If a beekeeper observes that a colony has completely vacated the hive, leaving behind all the honey and brood, this event is technically referred to as:

options.B: Reproductive division

questions.explanation: Absconding is specifically defined as when the queen and all other bees leave a hive completely, abandoning all their stores.

questions.stem: During a dearth period, a beekeeper provides sugar syrup to the bees. What is the primary purpose of this supplementary feeding?

options.A: To directly increase the honey harvest for the current season
options.B: To change the flavor of the stored honey
options.C: To prevent the bees from swarming away or absconding due to food scarcity
options.D: To attract pests like ants and wax moths into the hive

questions.explanation: Supplementary feeding during a dearth period prevents bees from swarming or absconding and ensures good future honey yield.

questions.stem: A beekeeper in Nigeria notices that his bees are most actively foraging and bringing nectar back to the hive in October. According to the seasonal calendar, this period is known as the:

options.B: Building up season

questions.explanation: The manual identifies September to November as the 'Nectar flow season' in the tropical region.

questions.stem: Which combination of smoking materials is suggested as being suitable for a smoker in the tropics?

options.B: Dried cow dung and maize cobs
options.C: Fresh green leaves and wet wood

questions.explanation: Dried cow dung and maize cobs are explicitly listed among the common smoking materials used in the tropics.

questions.stem: If a beekeeper accidentally uses a hot smoker or provides inadequate smoke during inspection, what is the most likely immediate reaction from the bees?

options.A: They will become calmer and easier to manage
options.B: They will become angry and more likely to sting
options.C: They will immediately start constructing new queen cells
options.D: They will begin the process of absconding

questions.explanation: A hot smoker or inadequate smoke is listed among the 'things that anger bees during inspection'.

questions.stem: A beekeeper has harvested honey and is now processing it. What is the only acceptable material for the storage containers to maintain quality?

options.B: Plastic or glass bottles

questions.explanation: The manual specifies that the only accepted materials for packaging honey are plastic and glass bottles, as metals react with the honey.

questions.stem: Based on the manual, which statement best summarizes the relative importance of pests versus diseases for a beekeeper in the tropics?

options.A: Diseases are the primary threat and should be the main focus of prevention
options.B: Pests and diseases are equally paramount and require the same level of attention
options.C: Pests should be adequately prevented, as diseases are less paramount
options.D: Neither pests nor diseases pose any significant risk to tropical bees

questions.explanation: The manual's note states: 'NB: diseases are less paramount in the tropics, pest should be adequately prevented.'

questions.stem: A beekeeper finds that their honey has started to ferment. What is the most probable cause based on the manual's guidelines?

options.A: The honey was stored in a plastic container
options.B: The honey was harvested during the building up season
options.C: The honey's moisture content was greater than 17%
options.D: The honey was not exposed to direct sunlight after harvesting

questions.explanation: The manual states the moisture content must not be greater than 17% to prevent fermentation.

questions.stem: Which entrepreneurial opportunity involves leveraging the bees' role in agriculture beyond the production of hive products?

options.B: Construction and marketing of beekeeping equipment

questions.explanation: This involves using bees to pollinate crops for other farmers, which is a service separate from selling physical bee products.

questions.stem: Why does the manual advise wearing a smooth white protective suit during inspection?

options.A: It absorbs heat and keeps the beekeeper cool
options.B: It helps to make the bees friendly and less likely to anger them
options.C: It is the cheapest color of suit available
options.D: It makes the beekeeper more visible to other people in the apiary

questions.explanation: Wearing a smooth white protective suit is listed as a way 'to make bees friendly during inspection'.

questions.stem: Which of the following baiting materials is NOT a direct product of the honey bee itself?

options.B: Bee wax

questions.explanation: Honey, wax, and propolis are all produced by bees. Palm wine juice is a plant-derived substance used to attract them.

questions.stem: If a beekeeper wants to harvest only the ripest, highest quality honey, which comb should they select?

options.B: Combs with a lot of open cells filled with watery liquid
options.C: Combs that are sealed or capped with wax
options.D: Combs that contain a large number of drone cells

questions.explanation: Maturity is indicated by the comb being sealed with wax. Only capped honey comb should be harvested.

questions.stem: A colony is consistently agitated and defensive. Upon inspection, the beekeeper cannot find the queen and notices no new eggs. According to the manual, what is likely agitating the bees?

options.A: Too much space in the hive
options.B: The absence of a queen
options.D: It is the honey flow season

questions.explanation: The absence of a queen is explicitly listed as one of the things that can anger bees during inspection.

questions.stem: Besides honey, the manual lists several other valuable hive products. Which of the following is known as a substance used by bees to seal cracks and sterilize the hive, and is also harvested for its medicinal properties?

options.B: Royal jelly

questions.explanation: Propolis is listed as a bee hive product and is used by bees for sealing and sterilization. It is also mentioned for its domestic, religious, and medicinal applications.

questions.stem: According to the guide, what is a necessary precaution to ensure the security of an apiary?

options.A: Placing it near a main road for easy access
options.B: Protecting it against bee enemies like honey badgers, ants, and human theft
options.C: Siting it in a low-lying area to avoid wind
options.D: Locating it near industrial areas for forage diversity

questions.explanation: Adequate security against enemies (animals, insects, and humans) is the very first factor listed for locating an apiary.

questions.stem: What is the main function of the 'queen substance' or pheromones produced by the queen bee?

options.B: To mark the entrance of the hive
options.C: To maintain the colony's cohesion and order
options.D: To signal the start of the honey flow season

questions.explanation: The text states the queen produces pheromones 'for maintaining the colony'.

questions.stem: During routine inspection, a beekeeper finds cells that are larger than normal and raised like a peanut shell. What are they most likely observing?

options.B: Honey storage cells

questions.explanation: The manual lists checking for 'Queen cells (occupied/unoccupied)' as a key thing to look for during inspection, as they are indicators of potential swarming.

questions.stem: A beekeeper wants to expand their operation by acquiring bees from an established feral colony living in a tree hollow. This method is known as:

options.B: Cluster harvesting

questions.explanation: Bee hunting is defined as collecting established feral colonies from their natural home, like a honeycomb in a tree.

questions.stem: What is the primary reason for using a hive tool during inspections?

options.B: To light the smoker
options.C: To pry apart frames or top bars that have been glued together with propolis
options.D: To sweep bees off the combs gently

questions.explanation: A hive tool is a standard implement used for separating hive components that bees have fastened together with propolis.

questions.stem: Which of the following scenarios would be the WORST timing for a beekeeper to open a hive for a thorough inspection?

options.A: A warm, sunny afternoon in December
options.B: A cool, cloudy, or rainy morning
options.C: During the peak of the honey flow in February
options.D: In the morning after the bees have started foraging

questions.explanation: Wrong timing, such as cold, cloudy, or rainy weather, is listed as an activity that can anger bees during inspection.

questions.stem: A potential beekeeper is concerned about the risks associated with livestock farming. How does beekeeping compare in terms of risk, according to the manual?

options.A: Beekeeping is significantly riskier than poultry farming
options.B: Beekeeping is less risky compared to poultry and other livestock ventures
options.C: Beekeeping carries the same level of risk as cattle ranching
options.D: The manual does not compare beekeeping to other ventures

questions.explanation: One of the listed benefits is that beekeeping is 'less risky compared to poultry and other livestock ventures'.

questions.stem: What is the immediate purpose of 'hive reversal' as a method to prevent swarming?

options.A: To confuse the bees and stop them from flying out
options.B: To create more space in the brood nest area
options.D: To expose the hive to more sunlight

questions.explanation: Hive reversal (swapping the position of brood boxes and honey supers) is a common management technique to alleviate overcrowding in the brood nest, a key swarming trigger.

questions.stem: If a drop of honey on a tabletop immediately flattens and spreads out like water, what does this suggest about its purity?

options.A: It is a sign of highly pure, high-quality honey
options.B: It is likely diluted or impure honey
options.C: It is pure honey with a low moisture content
options.D: It has been properly processed and filtered

questions.explanation: One tip for identifying pure honey is that it maintains an oval shape on a surface for a long period without spreading like water.

questions.stem: According to the information provided, what social benefit does beekeeping offer that makes it particularly suitable for community development?

options.A: It requires a high level of formal education
options.B: It is an all-gender inclusive venture that can be kept by women and men of all ages
options.C: It can only be practiced by young, strong men
options.D: It forces communities to clear large areas of forest

questions.explanation: The manual states beekeeping 'can be kept by women and men of all ages-all gender inclusive venture'.

questions.stem: A beekeeper notices overcrowding in the hive during the building-up season. If no action is taken, what is the most likely biological outcome?

options.B: Immediate death of the drones

questions.explanation: Overcrowding is a major predisposing factor for swarming, which is a reproductive process.

questions.stem: Which combination of factors would most likely lead to absconding rather than swarming?

options.A: Overcrowding and emergence of a new queen
options.B: Persistent disturbance, food shortage, and excessive heat
options.C: Presence of queen cells and abundant nectar
options.D: Strong floral resources and adequate ventilation

questions.explanation: Environmental stressors such as disturbance, hunger, and high temperature can cause the entire colony to abandon the hive (absconding).

questions.stem: Why is harvesting uncapped honey comb discouraged even during the official honey flow season?

options.B: It increases the number of drones
options.C: It may contain immature honey with unsafe moisture content

questions.explanation: Only capped comb indicates mature honey with moisture not exceeding 17%.

questions.stem: If a beekeeper stands directly in front of the hive entrance during inspection, which behavioral principle explains the likely aggressive response?

options.A: Blocking the bees' flight path causes defensive reaction
options.B: Bees dislike human shadows

questions.explanation: Standing in the flight path is listed as an activity that angers bees during inspection.

questions.stem: During the dearth season (April-June), what management priority should a beekeeper focus on?

options.B: Providing supplementary feeding where necessary

questions.explanation: Dearth season involves scarcity of nectar and pollen; supplementary feeding prevents swarming or absconding.

questions.stem: A colony has abundant nectar, an active queen, and warm weather. What is the expected behavioral state of the bees during inspection?

options.B: Calm and manageable

questions.explanation: Conducive atmosphere, nectar abundance, and active queen make bees friendlier during inspection.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why beekeeping is environmentally friendly?

options.A: It requires deforestation for hive placement
options.B: It improves pollination and sustains ecosystems

questions.explanation: Beekeeping maintains and sustains natural ecosystems through pollination without degrading land.

questions.stem: If honey is stored in a metal container and changes color and texture, what underlying principle explains this change?

options.B: Mineral reaction between metal and honey

questions.explanation: Metals cause mineral reactions that destroy honey texture, color, and quality.

questions.stem: Which management action directly addresses overcrowding as a trigger for swarming?

options.B: Hive reversal

questions.explanation: Hive reversal helps relieve overcrowding in brood areas, reducing swarming tendency.

questions.stem: A beekeeper observes queen cells but ignores them. Which long-term outcome is most probable?

options.B: Natural division of the colony into two groups

questions.explanation: Queen cells are indicators of swarming; failure to manage them may lead to colony division.

questions.stem: Which of the following best distinguishes a pest from a disease in the manual?

options.A: Pests are environmental conditions; diseases are insects
options.B: Pests are external organisms invading the hive; diseases are infections affecting bees
options.C: Pests increase honey yield; diseases reduce it

questions.explanation: Pests like ants and wax moth invade externally, while diseases such as nosema affect bee health internally.

questions.stem: Why is inspection important beyond honey production?

options.B: To detect disease or pest infection early
options.C: To reduce the need for smokers

questions.explanation: Routine inspection helps detect disease infection early and prevent swarming.

questions.stem: Which scenario best represents 'resilient income' as described in the manual?

options.A: Income that depends entirely on imported equipment
options.B: Income that continues even after displacement or disaster
options.C: Income generated only during honey flow season

questions.explanation: Beekeeping provides sustainable and steady income for displaced people and disaster victims.

questions.stem: If bees are killed or handled roughly during inspection, what chain reaction is most likely?

options.B: Release of alarm signals leading to aggression

questions.explanation: Killing bees and rough handling are listed as activities that anger bees.

questions.stem: Which of the following represents vertical value addition in beekeeping?

options.B: Processing and packaging honey for higher market value

questions.explanation: Value addition increases income beyond raw honey production.
